change.title: Make tapping an example video take you to your message (instead of just playing it)
change.targets: In-app occasion/examples screen -- role picked -> reached the create/message screen (#buyerSection / #receiverSection in index.html)
change.expected_effect: A few more role-committed users per fortnight reach the create screen (and, at 86% press-through, a finished video and the in-app review ask). Small in absolute terms and below the noise floor; valuable because it is the highest per-head review slice and compounds.
change.why_it_helps: On this screen the most obvious thing to tap -- the example video -- used to just play a clip and leave people stuck, while the real 'next' buttons were small or buried. About a quarter of people who pick a role never get past this screen. Making the card itself move them forward, with the example's words already filled in, gives ready customers one clear tap toward finishing their video -- and a finished video is what leads to the review ask.
changes_in_plain_words: Tapping an example video card now takes you straight to the message screen with that example's words already filled in -- before, tapping the card just played the clip and left you on the same screen.
Each card now has a clear gold 'Use this ->' button so the next step is obvious.
You can still watch any example first -- the little play button on the video is still there.
The big 'Create from Scratch' button became a calm 'or write your own message' link underneath, so there's one obvious way forward and one quiet alternative.

previews.label: The 'choose your vibe' screen after someone taps 'I Received This Gift'
The 'choose your occasion' screen after someone taps "I'm Giving This Gift"

change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: Users who convert here are ready to make the video and manage to find the forward action; they get a fast path to a pre-filled, on-brand message they can send in one more tap. The occasion screen asks nothing in exchange -- it is not a gate, it is a routing screen whose only job is to pick which template pre-fills the box. So the rate is not a price being accepted; it is pure navigation efficiency, which is why an affordance fix (not a motivation or exchange change) is the right lever: there is no reward being withheld to protect.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A non-trivial share of the 23% who stall on the occasion screen do so because the forward action is unclear (not purely because they lost interest).
Making the card tap advance does not frustrate users who wanted to preview -- mitigated by keeping an explicit visible play control and the Back button.

Landing on the message screen with a pre-filled template (rather than an autoplay video) is not a downgrade in perceived payoff -- the pre-filled message and the retained preview keep the value visible.
The template pre-fill and swapNamePlaceholder path (already used by useTemplate/applyPendingTemplate) works when triggered from a card-body tap.
change.second_order_effects: Advancing on card tap will shift the mix from 'Create from Scratch' toward template-based entries (template_used up, from-scratch down) -- harmless; templates are on-brand starting points. Some users who currently tap to preview will now advance instead; if they only wanted to watch, they can still tap the explicit play control or press Back -- and advancing is not a commitment (no video is generated until they press Create on the next screen, 86% likely once there). Downstream: this touches only the in-app occasion screen; email capture (claim page, upstream), the discount code, and video-by-email delivery are all untouched, and reviews via email_redirect are 0 in both windows -- so no review-reminder cost. The only review path this feeds is the in-app thank-you screen, which this change helps by getting more role-committed users to a finished video.
change.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the 77% vs 86% split is within noise (13 vs 6 people), the brainstorm picked the create button for a reason, and you are second-guessing the slate on a coin-flip; worse, making the card advance REMOVES the pre-commit video preview that is the only place users feel the payoff, so you might depress motivation and lose more than you gain. My answer: I am not ranking on the WoW delta -- I rank on the LEVEL (the occasion-screen drop is the larger half in BOTH windows, 13 and 12 vs 6 and 9) combined with never-touched status and a concrete code-verified affordance flaw, which the create button (already 86%, one engaged replay pressed it in 4s) does not have. And I explicitly PRESERVE the preview: every card keeps a visible play control, so the payoff stays one tap away -- it demotes the video from 'accidental dead-end' to 'deliberate preview', which is strictly clearer, not a removal. If it re-measures flat, the honest read is 'affordance was not the binding constraint / interest ceiling', not a claimed win -- the entry ships labelled unmeasurable-by-design.

tradeoff.gained: More role-committed users find the forward action and reach Create -> finished video -> the in-app thank-you review ask (the only surface producing reviews -- 9/9 in_app this window). Highest per-head review value in the review journey.
tradeoff.risked: The pre-commit example video becomes a deliberate tap (via the play control) rather than the default card action, so some passive previewing is lost; if any of the 23% were a genuine interest ceiling, they will not be recovered. No measurable downstream cost: review clicks via email_redirect (Klaviyo reminders) are 0 in both windows, and email capture / code / video delivery are all upstream and untouched.
unverified_assumptions: That a non-trivial share of occasion-screen stalls are affordance confusion rather than a post-role interest ceiling -- the instruments are blind between role-select and reaching the create screen, so this cannot be proven at this traffic.

change.differs_from_past_attempt: The occasion/examples screen has NEVER been attacked (coverage map). Not the 2026-07-06 message-step fix (that changed the textarea DEFAULT and removed the NAME alert on a DIFFERENT screen, #createSection). Not PR #8 or either 2026-07-23 ship (all claim-page). Not the 2026-08-01 welcome re-rank (welcome screen, above role-pick, freshly fenced). It does NOT develop the recommended slate angle (sticky Create button) because the evidence shows the create-screen sub-step is already 86% -- the smaller half of the leak; it develops the occasion-screen angle the brainstorm flagged as the strongest alternative on a never-touched surface. No owner rejection touches this screen (both rejections are claim-page/review-ask items).

pr_body:
## What this changes

Inside the video-maker, after someone chooses whether they gave or received the gift, they land on a 'choose your occasion / choose your vibe' screen with three example videos. Until now the most obvious thing to tap -- the example video card -- only *played* the clip and left the person stuck on the same screen. The two ways to actually move forward were easy to miss: a small muted 'Customize Template' button on each card, and a loud 'Create from Scratch' button below an 'or' line.

This change flips that so the obvious tap is the forward one:

1. **Tapping an example card now takes you straight to the message screen** with that example's words already filled in.
2. Each card gets a clear gold **'Use this ->'** button.
3. You can **still watch any example first** -- the play button on the video stays.
4. **'Create from Scratch'** becomes a calm **'or write your own message'** link, so there's one obvious way forward and one quiet alternative.

Nothing was removed or gated: no video is made until the next screen, and the email, discount and video delivery all sit elsewhere and are untouched.

## Why this screen

Using person-by-person data in PostHog across two 14-day windows, about a quarter of people who pick a role never reach the message screen: **77% (43 of 56)** got there this window, **75% (36 of 48)** the window before -- a steady ~23-25% who stall right here. That's the bigger, steadier half of the drop, and this screen had **never been worked on before**. The smaller half (reaching the screen but not pressing the Create button) is already at **86% (37 of 43)**, so the button is not where the big loss is. Everyone who gets past this screen is in the part of the review journey that actually produces reviews -- reviews arrive ~100% from the in-app 'thank you' screen after a finished video (9 of 9 this window, 0 from reminder emails; same pattern the prior window), so recovering these people is the highest-value slice we have.

## Honest note on measurability

At ~56 role-pickers per fortnight, a few extra people is **too small to prove** -- swings under ~13-20 points can't be told apart from luck at this traffic. So this ships **labelled 'unmeasurable by design'** and will **never be called a win without a statistically significant result**. The one thing we can't prove: whether people stall here because the forward step was unclear, or because some simply lost interest after picking a role -- our tools are blind between those two moments. The change is low-risk and fully reversible either way, and the dead-end tap was a real design defect regardless.

## Last change's verdict

The 2026-08-01 change (leading the claim-arrival welcome with the create invitation) stays **not measurable by design / pending**. For transparency: the metric it aimed at (arrived in app -> started a video) moved 31.6% (30 of 95) -> 40.7% (37 of 91), +9.1 points, but `node tools/significance.mjs 30 95 37 91` returns **p=0.20, NOT SIGNIFICANT** -- indistinguishable from noise, so it is **not** claimed as a win. Direction is encouraging on both its targets; nothing can be claimed.

## The ranked drops this cycle

1. **Occasion screen: pick a role -> reach the message screen -- 77% (43/56), was 75% (36/48).** The bigger, steadier, never-touched half. **Chosen.**
2. Message screen: reach it -> press Create -- 86% (37/43). Smaller and noisier; only 6 people lost.
3. Claim page: land -> give email -- 43% (61/141). Biggest by raw headcount but flat, already worked three times, and feeds reviews weakly per head.

## Reviewer's verdict and how I responded

An independent auditor **approved** the plan with two minor notes. (1) Two of my sources disagreed on the exact review count (10/8 vs 9/9) -- I reconciled to the frozen 9/9 figure; it changes nothing, since both agree ~100% of reviews come from the in-app thank-you screen and none from reminder emails. (2) The assumed cause is a well-grounded bet, not a proven fact -- acknowledged, carried forward in the report, and the change ships labelled unmeasurable and is fully reversible.

## How I verified it

Parsed the page's JavaScript (no syntax errors), booted the app locally, and confirmed the live page returns 200 with every change present and the old buttons gone. Rendered before/after mobile screenshots of both roles' occasion screens (attached). No test data was written -- the screenshot tool blocked all tracking calls.

## What to re-measure, and when

Around **2026-08-29** (both windows on or after 2026-08-15), re-run the person-linked PostHog step from picking a role to reaching the message screen for both frozen windows, then run the significance test. Also watch whether more people now start from a template than 'from scratch' (expected, and harmless). **Never call it a win without a significant result.**
